messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV-2 - partial console <-> dataplane mismatch detected for live routing. Impact: some customers see stale route state in Console while API returns current state. Pager: @oncall-ryan. Please ack and start triage. :rotating_light:
oncall-ryan: Acked. I'm joining bridge. Quick ask: which regions are affected?
anika: I'm seeing errors in the console shard logs for region-us-west-2. Frontend shows routes stuck at v42 while API shows v44.
micha: Confirmed. Metrics: increase in 5xx proxy errors to console from control-plane starting ~1967889900. Sending logs in a sec.
sre-ops-bot: Auto-attach: runbook: live-isolation-playbook v1.2. Recommended initial actions: 1) check controlplane config propagation, 2) validate feature-flag rollout, 3) isolate dataplane to prevent further drift.
oncall-ryan: On bridge: https://meet.redwood/in/incident-1967 if people want to join.
emily: Customer-impact quick assessment: 12 customers (mostly mid-tier) reported UI inconsistencies, 3 customers filed support tickets about stale routing in the console. No API-only failures reported.
tariq: Hypothesis 1: flag propagation race - feature flag gating config push to some console regions. Hypothesis 2: control-plane metadata lag due to batching - seq numbers out of order.
anika: Pasting relevant log snippet from console-proxy-usw2 (truncated):
```
2026-06-11T18:05:45Z console-proxy[pid=4428] WARN route-sync: expected seq=44 got seq=42, rejecting update
2026-06-11T18:05:46Z console-proxy[pid=4428] INFO route-cache: applying local delta from seq=42
2026-06-11T18:06:02Z control-plane[pid=2231] INFO route-publish: published seq=44 to region-us-west-2
2026-06-11T18:06:05Z console-proxy[pid=4428] ERROR sync-failure: missing ack for seq=44
```
micha: Also seeing control-plane publish logs showing retries to push to edge mux: `push_routes(region=us-west-2, seq=44) -> timeout on attempt 3`
oncall-ryan: Can someone check the propagation queue sizes and any backpressure?
sre-ops-bot: Queue metrics: controlplane->dataplane queue depth US-WEST-2: 0/512 but mux retry count spike seen 18:05:40-18:06:10.
emily: Support note: advising customers to refresh console; UI workaround seems to surface updated state after manual refresh, but still flaky for some. Documenting outreach to top-3 impacted customers.
tariq: Quick check: were any rollout flags toggled in the last hour? 
anika: Yes — `optimize-routing-v2` rollout started 18:00 UTC with 10% canary, then 50% at 18:04, rolled back to 10% at 18:07 in response to perf anomaly.
micha: That aligns. Rollout could have caused inconsistent config snapshots across control-plane replicas.
oncall-ryan: Mitigation plan: 1) pause any ongoing rollouts (anika), 2) force a full resync for console proxies in affected regions (micha), 3) enable bypass for mux retries to push immediate updates (tariq), 4) update customer comms (emily).
anika: Pausing rollouts now. Patch: `kubectl rollout pause deploy/flag-manager -n controlplane` -> success.
micha: Starting resync: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/regions/us-west-2/force-resync -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'` -> 202 Accepted. Watching logs.
tariq: Enabling bypass: toggling `mux_force_push=true` at control-plane config. Applying now.
```
# config change
PATCH /api/v1/config
body: {"mux_force_push": true}
```
oncall-ryan: While we apply changes, let's capture timeline for RCA. I'll create a short bullet timeline here.
- 18:00 UTC: `optimize-routing-v2` rollout starts (canary 10%)
- 18:04 UTC: rollout increases to 50%
- 18:05:40 UTC: control-plane publishes seq=44 for us-west-2; mux reports timeouts
- 18:05:45 UTC: console-proxy logs indicate expected seq mismatch
- 18:06:05 UTC: mux retries spike, some proxies fail to ack
- 18:07 UTC: rollback to 10% triggered manually
- 18:09 UTC: rollouts paused, force-resync and mux bypass applied
- 18:12 UTC: customers start reporting manual refresh fixes
- 18:20 UTC: monitoring shows decreased retry rate and ack stabilizing

emily: I'll draft a short update for affected customers summarizing mitigation and ETA for RCA.
tariq: Quick data ask: can someone grab network stats between control-plane and mux gate at 18:05-18:07? wondering if transient network blips caused retries.
micha: Attaching netstat excerpt (timestamps aligned):
```
2026-06-11T18:05:38Z tcp_conn(region=us-west-2) established=120 rtt_ms=12
2026-06-11T18:05:41Z tcp_conn(region=us-west-2) established=119 rtt_ms=200  # transient spike
2026-06-11T18:05:44Z tcp_conn(region=us-west-2) established=118 rtt_ms=15
```
anika: So we have a small RTT spike at 18:05:41 which coincides with push timeout window. Could be contributing.
oncall-ryan: Hypotheses ranked: 1) Flag rollout caused inconsistent snapshots + transient mux timeout exacerbated -> missed ack leading to console stale state. 2) Network jitter alone caused mux retries and state mismatch.
emily: Impact classification draft: partial UI inconsistency, low data loss risk, higher ops overhead. Recommend SEV-2->SEV-3 downgrade after stabilization and customer comms.
tariq: For RCA, we should capture: rollout gating logic, seq id handling (idempotency), retry/backoff windows, and whether resync on push failure is immediate or delayed.
micha: I'll collect control-plane replica logs and mux ACK traces and drop into the incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1967890123/logs/
anika: Also saving console-proxy heap and cache snapshots for affected nodes.
oncall-ryan: Good. Next steps: 1) follow-up bridge at +30 for status, 2) prepare rollback reversal plan if resync doesn't converge, 3) Emily to send customer msg. I'll update incident doc with these notes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident note: timeline and mitigation steps recorded; suggested postmortem template: https://go.redwood/incident-postmortem
emily: Sent customer update to affected list — short, we will follow up with RCA in 48h.
micha: Monitoring shows mux retry rate dropped to baseline at 18:18 UTC. Console seq acks normalizing now.
oncall-ryan: Downgrading pager to SEV-3; still monitoring. Closing bridge in 5.
emily: I'll track RCA action items and assign owners in the postmortem doc.
end of thread
